smells.finding: thresholds_for is 3 executable lines; _gate_headroom_tokens is 8; neither call site grew a branch. Body length is unchanged, only docstrings grew.
No class was touched on the production side; the two new test classes are cohesive (resolver / trip-integration) and split along that seam.

The composition `_gauge_reader.thresholds_for(reading.model, _gate_headroom_tokens(cl, <gate>))` is written out twice -- checklist_engine.py:1485-1486 (_trip_advisory) and :1542-1543 (_trip_hard_band_reading). The gate's whole point (c) is that these two must resolve the SAME number, yet sameness is currently held by convention across two copies rather than by a single expression. Extracting one private helper (e.g. `_thresholds_for_gate(cl, model, gate)`) would make 'shown == judged' structural instead of conventional, and would delete mutation M11/M12's entire failure mode. NON-BLOCKING: 2 occurrences, both covered by the together-sweep test.

_gate_headroom_tokens touches only the checklist dict it is given and computes no threshold, honouring constraint:no-threshold-values; the arithmetic stays in gauge_reader, which owns the window and the caps.
(cl, base_dir, gate) now travels together through _trip_advisory / _trip_hard_band_reading / _trip_hard_gate -- a three-item clump that a small context object would absorb.

override.repo_standard: checklist_engine.py's Trip-section convention, stated at the advance call site (:2856-2858): 'The band decision belongs to this CLI boundary, so `advance` stays a pure function of its arguments and every direct caller is unaffected.' Reinforced by global-crew.md 'no hidden fallback; fail visibly. Keep state and side effects obvious and contained.'
override.reason: The explicit-argument style is what makes these functions pure and directly unit-testable without a fixture object, and it is what let the neighbour-isolation tests call _trip_hard_band_reading(cl, path, 'reconcile') by name. A context object would hide which gate is being judged -- the exact fact DC4 requires the tests to state out loud.

smells.finding: The reserve is a bare int token count threaded through three functions rather than a named Reserve/Headroom type; `thresholds_for`'s parameter is annotated `float` while the only shipped producer returns `int`.

override.repo_standard: decision:gate-headroom-absolute-tokens (@grade: settled/measured, named in the g3 handoff's map anchors): the override is an absolute-token reserve in the SAME unit as _PROFILES' caps, because context-rot degradation tracks absolute token count. Plus decision:no-config-tier's stated reasoning that a seam with one hypothetical adapter is a guess, not a boundary.
override.reason: A wrapper type would introduce exactly the one-user seam decision:no-config-tier already rejected on this gate, and the unit is already pinned by being identical to the caps it is subtracted from. The float/int annotation mismatch is a minor precision nit, recorded as a non-blocking observation in the review result rather than a smell worth restructuring for.

smells.finding: The longest new signature is _trip_hard_band_reading(cl, base_dir, gate=None) -- three, one of them defaulted. thresholds_for went from one parameter to two.
The opposite of shotgun surgery is what shipped: one resolver, one arithmetic site, two call sites. Adding a reserve to another gate is a one-line data edit in a template, changed in no code.
thresholds_for changes for one reason (threshold arithmetic); _gate_headroom_tokens changes for one reason (where the key is read from). The diff does not add a second axis of change to either.
`(cl.get('tasks') or {}).get(gate)` is a two-step guarded dict lookup on one owned structure, not a chain of asks across objects.

Actively resisted rather than merely avoided: no checklist-config tier was built (decision:no-config-tier), no adapter/seam was introduced, and the mechanism is exercised exactly once by real shipped data. `headroom_tokens=0` and `gate=None` are backward-compatibility defaults with existing callers, not hypothetical extension points.

The comment-to-code ratio in the diff is extreme: thresholds_for is 3 executable lines under a 30-line docstring; _gate_headroom_tokens is 8 lines under a 20-line docstring; the spine template carries a 350-word context_headroom_note beside a 5-character value.

override.repo_standard: global-crew.md: 'Match the surrounding code's naming, labeling, and in-file documentation conventions -- the project's specific conventions are the local delta.' The surrounding Trip section (checklist_engine.py :1200-1600) and gauge_reader.py's _PROFILES block use exactly this why-carrying-docstring form. CREW_CONTEXT.md 'Verification Discipline' additionally requires the WHY behind a guard to be recoverable, and the two-bin rule (GLOSSARY) makes the note the only place a @grade: guess can be recorded for later revision.
override.reason: The prose is not hiding an unclear implementation -- the code under each docstring is trivially readable. It carries the safety ARGUMENT (why two clamps, not one), the decision anchors, and the honest 'this is a GUESS' label for 30000, which the shipped test asserts is present. Deleting it would delete the only durable record of decision:execute-gate-reserve-value's grade. Verified specifically that the prose is not doing a test's job: every property the docstrings claim is separately asserted by a named test and killed by a named mutation (M1-M16), which is the CREW_CONTEXT rule 'assert against behaviour, never against text that describes it'.
